checks.mechanism_accuracy: passed — Kubernetes is the service/lifecycle control plane over heterogeneous infrastructure while Slurm remains the independent execution backend for tightly coupled and training workloads
checks.old_path_rationale: passed — remote batch HPC remains reasonable for long static training jobs whose handoff ends at a checkpoint
checks.changed_constraint: passed — fine-tuning, persistent inference, continuous evaluation and artifact proliferation require lifecycle governance beyond a batch-job boundary
checks.state_data_control_ownership: passed — lifecycle identity/evidence/rollout belong to the production control plane while fabric, scheduler, storage and failure-domain owners remain distinct
checks.gain_and_cost: passed — fewer cross-system lifecycle handoffs are balanced against common-storage, network, scheduler-interoperability, HA, authorization and coupled-failure-domain work
checks.failure_fallback_coexistence: passed — unfinished common storage, realistic inference characterization, isolation and SLO evidence keep the design at evolving-pilot status; bifurcated batch HPC plus serving remains the fallback/coexisting architecture
checks.evidence_boundary: passed — the prose does not claim universal superiority and the Review note preserves pilot status, unfinished work and undisclosed portable SLO/multitenant/cross-facility evidence
checks.owner_and_chapter_coherence: passed — the delta extends the immutable-revision Production Contract and transitions directly into Readiness Gates; adjacent Security and Prompt chapters retain their own trust and Agent-input ownership
checks.placement: passed — mechanism body and marker are before Review notes; no mechanism body for this family appears after Review notes
checks.non_list_prose: passed — integrated as an old-boundary-to-hybrid-control-plane-to-trade-off reasoning chain, not a paper list

items.adversarial_boundary_note: The exact-v1 explicitly calls the deployed arrangement dual-control-plane and keeps fine-tuning compute on Slurm. The Books heading refers only to a unified lifecycle control plane; its body preserves distinct execution substrates and scheduler authority, so it does not collapse the two control planes or claim a completed all-Kubernetes training stack. End-to-end artifact identity/evidence is presented as the chapter's normative Production Contract, not as a measured paper result.
